title: Walking for bigger bodies: how to start without knee pain
intro: Walking is the easiest and safest way to start moving, even if you weigh 100 kg or more. The key is to start short and slow, then add a little at a time so your knees can get used to it.
muscles: Legs (calves, thighs, glutes), heart and lungs. It also helps your knee and hip joints get used to moving. Walking supports overall energy burn together with your eating, not fat burning in just one spot.
steps: Wear comfortable shoes with cushioning, not slippers.
Choose a flat route like your home corridor, a park, or inside an air-conditioned mall.
Walk with short, comfortable steps, body upright, shoulders relaxed.
Let your heel land first, then roll through to your toes.
Walk at a pace where you can still talk without gasping.
After your session, walk slowly for 1-2 minutes before sitting down.
mistakes: Walking 45 minutes straight on day one, then your knees hurt and you stop for a week.
Taking steps that are too long or too fast. This adds pressure on your knees.
Walking uphill or on stairs too early, before your body is ready.
easier: Start with just 5 minutes, or break it into 3 rounds of 3-5 minutes a day (for example after breakfast, during your office break, after dinner). You can also march on the spot while holding onto a chair or wall.
harder: Add 2-3 minutes every week until you reach 30 minutes. Once comfortable, try walking a bit faster for 1 minute, then slower for 2 minutes, and repeat a few times. Still no jumping or running.
dose: Weeks 1-2: 5-10 minutes, 3-5 days a week. Slowly build up to 20-30 minutes a day, 5 days a week. You can split it into a few short sessions.
safety: Stop if your knees, hips or feet feel sharp pain, or if you feel dizzy, very short of breath or have chest pain. If you have heart problems, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or recently had surgery, see a doctor first before starting.

faq.q: My knees feel a bit achy after walking. Is that normal?
faq.a: Mild aching that goes away in a day or two is usually normal when your body is just starting to move. But if there is sharp pain, swelling, or it keeps getting worse, cut down your walking time and get advice from a doctor or physio.

faq.q: Do I need to hit 10,000 steps a day?
faq.a: No need. If you walk 2,000 steps now, try going up to 3,000 first. Adding a little at a time is better than chasing a big number and getting injured.

faq.q: Is walking alone enough to lose weight?
faq.a: Walking helps, but weight loss comes from a combination of eating and movement. You can still eat rice, just watch your plate size and how often. Walking helps your energy and overall health.
